quizQuestions.question: Which principle does a stack data structure follow?
quizQuestions.explanation: A stack follows the Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle.

quizQuestions.question: Which principle does a standard queue data structure follow?
quizQuestions.explanation: A standard queue operates on a First In, First Out (FIFO) basis.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time complexity to access an element by index in an array?
quizQuestions.explanation: Arrays provide direct memory addressing, allowing constant time O(1) access.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time complexity to insert a node at the head of a singly linked list?
quizQuestions.explanation: Inserting at the head only requires updating the head pointer, taking O(1) time.

quizQuestions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), how does the left child compare to its parent?
quizQuestions.explanation: By definition, the left child of a BST node must hold a smaller value.

quizQuestions.question: Which binary tree has all leaf nodes at the same level and every internal node has two children?
quizQuestions.explanation: A perfect binary tree is completely filled at all levels.

quizQuestions.question: What is the technical term for a node in a graph data structure?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nodes in a graph are called vertices, and connections are called edges.

quizQuestions.question: Which element is always located at the root of a Min-Heap?
quizQuestions.explanation: In a min-heap, the parent node is always smaller than or equal to its children.

quizQuestions.question: What occurs when two distinct keys map to the same index in a hash table?
quizQuestions.explanation: A collision occurs when a hash function maps two different keys to the same bucket.

quizQuestions.question: Which mathematical operator is commonly used to implement a circular queue?
quizQuestions.explanation: The modulo operator wraps indices around the array boundaries.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure manages function call frames during program execution?
quizQuestions.explanation: The runtime call stack tracks active function calls and local variables.

quizQuestions.question: What type of data structure is an AVL tree?
quizQuestions.explanation: An AVL tree is a height-balanced binary search tree that automatically rebalances.

quizQuestions.question: How many pointers does each node contain in a standard doubly linked list?
quizQuestions.explanation: Each node maintains two pointers: one to the next node and one to the previous node.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure is best suited for converting an infix expression to postfix?
quizQuestions.explanation: A stack manages operator precedence and parentheses during parsing.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure is typically used to implement an efficient priority queue?
quizQuestions.explanation: A binary heap provides O(log n) insertions and extractions for priority queues.

quizQuestions.question: In which domain are B-Trees most commonly used?
quizQuestions.explanation: B-Trees are optimized for disk systems and widely used in database indices.

quizQuestions.question: What is the node visit sequence in an inorder traversal of a binary tree?
quizQuestions.explanation: Inorder traversal visits the left subtree first, then the root, then the right subtree.

quizQuestions.question: What sequence is produced by an inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree?
quizQuestions.explanation: Inorder traversal of a valid BST visits keys in strictly ascending order.

quizQuestions.question: Which representation is most space-efficient for storing a dense graph?
quizQuestions.explanation: An adjacency matrix provides O(1) edge lookup without pointer overhead in dense graphs.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary application of a Trie data structure?
quizQuestions.explanation: Tries store strings associatively, making prefix lookups and autocomplete very efficient.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure supports insertion and deletion at both ends in O(1) time?
quizQuestions.explanation: A double-ended queue (deque) allows push and pop operations at both ends.

quizQuestions.question: What color must the root node always have in a standard Red-Black Tree?
quizQuestions.explanation: By definition, the root of a Red-Black Tree must be black.

quizQuestions.question: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (root at height 0)?
quizQuestions.explanation: A binary tree of height h can contain up to 2^(h+1) - 1 nodes.

quizQuestions.question: Which structure is used in separate chaining to resolve hash table collisions?
quizQuestions.explanation: Separate chaining resolves collisions by storing colliding items in a linked list per bucket.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure is used to detect cycles efficiently in Kruskal's algorithm?
quizQuestions.explanation: DSU maintains sets of connected vertices to test for cycles in near-constant time.

quizQuestions.question: What condition must be satisfied before applying Binary Search on an array?
choices: The array size must be a power of two
quizQuestions.explanation: Binary search relies on sorted ordering to eliminate half the search space each step.

quizQuestions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Merge Sort?
quizQuestions.explanation: Merge sort divides the array evenly and takes O(n log n) time in all cases.

quizQuestions.question: When does Quick Sort exhibit its worst-case time complexity of O(n^2)?
choices: When the chosen pivot is an extreme value
When the pivot is the exact median
When the input array is randomly ordered
quizQuestions.explanation: Choosing the minimum or maximum element repeatedly causes severely unbalanced partitions.

quizQuestions.question: What is the best-case time complexity of an optimized Bubble Sort on a sorted array?
quizQuestions.explanation: A swapped flag allows the algorithm to terminate after a single O(n) scan.

quizQuestions.question: On which type of graph does Dijkstra's algorithm fail to produce correct shortest paths?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dijkstra assumes distances are monotonically non-decreasing and fails with negative edges.

quizQuestions.question: What are the two core properties required to apply Dynamic Programming?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dynamic programming requires optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure is standard for implementing Breadth-First Search (BFS)?
quizQuestions.explanation: BFS uses a FIFO queue to visit graph nodes level by level.

quizQuestions.question: Which data structure or mechanism is standard for Depth-First Search (DFS)?
quizQuestions.explanation: DFS explores deeply along each branch using an explicit or call stack.

quizQuestions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search on an array of size n?
quizQuestions.explanation: Linear search may inspect every element in the array, requiring O(n) comparisons.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is inherently stable?
quizQuestions.explanation: Merge sort preserves the relative order of elements with equal keys.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithmic paradigm provides an optimal solution for the Fractional Knapsack problem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Sorting items by value-to-weight ratio yields an optimal greedy solution.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithmic technique is standard for solving the 0/1 Knapsack problem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Because items cannot be split, optimal subproblems are combined via dynamic programming.

quizQuestions.question: What primary capability does Bellman-Ford have over Dijkstra's algorithm?
choices: It correctly handles negative edge weights
Its time complexity is O(log n)
quizQuestions.explanation: Bellman-Ford handles negative weights and detects negative weight cycles.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithm is used to find a Minimum Spanning Tree of a connected weighted graph?
quizQuestions.explanation: Prim's algorithm greedily expands a tree to find a minimum spanning tree.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithm finds shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a weighted graph?
quizQuestions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall solves the all-pairs shortest path problem in O(V^3) time.

quizQuestions.question: Which type of graph is required to produce a valid Topological Sort?
quizQuestions.explanation: Topological sorting requires directed edges without any directed cycles.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithm finds the maximum subarray sum in O(n) time?
quizQuestions.explanation: Kadane's algorithm computes the maximum contiguous subarray sum in a single linear pass.

quizQuestions.question: Under what condition is the two-pointer technique most effective on an array?
choices: When the array contains random elements
quizQuestions.explanation: Sorted order allows the two pointers to make deterministic directional decisions.

quizQuestions.question: What type of data compression does Huffman Coding perform?
quizQuestions.explanation: Huffman coding generates variable-length prefix codes without losing any information.

quizQuestions.question: Which theorem provides asymptotic bounds for divide-and-conquer recurrence relations?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Master Theorem solves recurrences of the form T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).

quizQuestions.question: What is the theoretical lower bound for comparison-based sorting algorithms?
quizQuestions.explanation: Decision tree analysis proves comparison sorting requires at least Omega(n log n) operations.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time complexity of Counting Sort for an array of size n with elements up to k?
quizQuestions.explanation: Counting sort runs in O(n + k) time by tallying frequencies directly.

quizQuestions.question: Which approach is standard for finding the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)?
quizQuestions.explanation: LCS uses a 2D dynamic programming grid to evaluate matching subproblems.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithmic technique is typically used to solve the N-Queens problem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Backtracking systematically explores placements and prunes invalid configurations.

quizQuestions.question: To which complexity class does the decision version of the Traveling Salesperson Problem belong?
quizQuestions.explanation: The decision version of the Traveling Salesperson Problem is NP-Complete.

quizQuestions.question: Which standard function is used in C to release dynamically allocated memory?
quizQuestions.explanation: The free() function deallocates memory previously allocated by malloc() or calloc().

quizQuestions.question: Which OOP concept bundles data and methods while restricting direct external access?
quizQuestions.explanation: Encapsulation hides internal state and exposes behavior only through public interfaces.

quizQuestions.question: Which Java virtual machine component automatically recovers unused heap memory?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Garbage Collector identifies and reclaims unreferenced heap objects.

quizQuestions.question: Which mechanism enables compile-time polymorphism in C++?
quizQuestions.explanation: Function and operator overloading resolve polymorphic calls during compilation.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following built-in data types in Python is immutable?
quizQuestions.explanation: Tuples cannot be modified after creation, making them immutable.

quizQuestions.question: What is the OOP mechanism where a new class adopts properties of an existing class?
quizQuestions.explanation: Inheritance allows subclasses to acquire fields and methods from superclasses.

quizQuestions.question: What does a pointer variable hold in C programming?
choices: The memory address of another variable
quizQuestions.explanation: A pointer stores the memory address where another value resides.

quizQuestions.question: Which construct allows a class to achieve multiple interface inheritance in Java?
quizQuestions.explanation: A Java class can implement multiple interfaces while extending only one class.

quizQuestions.question: Which keyword creates a small anonymous inline function in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: The lambda keyword defines anonymous, single-expression functions in Python.

quizQuestions.question: Which keyword is declared in a C++ base class to enable dynamic runtime dispatch?
quizQuestions.explanation: The virtual keyword instructs C++ to use a vtable for runtime method dispatch.

quizQuestions.question: What is the execution architecture of standard client-side JavaScript engines?
quizQuestions.explanation: JavaScript uses a single execution thread paired with an event loop for asynchronous tasks.

quizQuestions.question: Which programming paradigm treats computation as evaluating mathematical functions without mutable state?
quizQuestions.explanation: Functional programming avoids state mutations and promotes pure mathematical functions.

quizQuestions.question: Where does the String Constant Pool reside in modern Java memory architectures?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Java String Constant Pool is allocated within the main heap space.

quizQuestions.question: When is a class constructor automatically invoked in object-oriented programming?
choices: When an object instance is created
quizQuestions.explanation: Constructors execute automatically when allocating and initializing a new instance.

quizQuestions.question: What is the default initial index for arrays in C?
quizQuestions.explanation: C arrays use zero-based indexing, where the first element is located at index 0.

quizQuestions.question: Which method appends an item to the end of an existing Python list?
quizQuestions.explanation: The append() method adds an element directly to the end of a list.

quizQuestions.question: What is it called when a child class provides a specific implementation of a parent method?
quizQuestions.explanation: Method overriding allows a derived class to supply its own logic for an inherited method.

quizQuestions.question: In which year was the C programming language originally developed by Dennis Ritchie?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie created C at Bell Labs in 1972.

quizQuestions.question: What is the role of the `finally` block in Java exception handling?
choices: Executes only when an exception occurs
quizQuestions.explanation: A finally block executes after try-catch blocks whether an exception was raised or not.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following cannot be used as a key in a standard Python dictionary?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dictionary keys must be hashable and immutable; lists are mutable.

quizQuestions.question: What is a dangling pointer in systems programming?
quizQuestions.explanation: A dangling pointer points to memory that has already been freed or deallocated.

quizQuestions.question: Which symbol precedes a class name when declaring a destructor in C++?
quizQuestions.explanation: A destructor is declared using a tilde (~) prefix before the class name.

quizQuestions.question: What does a static variable belong to in a Java class?
quizQuestions.explanation: Static members belong to the class rather than to any individual object instance.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary advantage of list comprehensions in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: List comprehensions offer a clean, expressive way to construct and transform lists.

quizQuestions.question: Why is a base case mandatory in any recursive function?
choices: To stop recursion and prevent stack overflow
quizQuestions.explanation: Without a base case, recursion continues indefinitely until the call stack overflows.

quizQuestions.question: What is the central core module of an operating system?
quizQuestions.explanation: The kernel is the core component that manages hardware and system resources.

quizQuestions.question: Which scheduling parameter is central to Round Robin CPU scheduling?
quizQuestions.explanation: Round Robin assigns each ready process a fixed time slice called a quantum.

quizQuestions.question: How many Coffman conditions must hold simultaneously for a deadlock to occur?
quizQuestions.explanation: All four conditions must hold: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.

quizQuestions.question: Which mechanism is primarily used to implement Virtual Memory in modern operating systems?
quizQuestions.explanation: Virtual memory relies on demand paging and address translation tables.

quizQuestions.question: What is the state called when an OS spends more time swapping pages than executing code?
quizQuestions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when constant page faults consume nearly all processing capacity.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Banker's Algorithm in operating systems?
quizQuestions.explanation: Banker's Algorithm tests for safe resource allocation states to avoid deadlocks.

quizQuestions.question: What information is stored inside a Process Control Block (PCB)?
choices: Process state, program counter, and CPU registers
quizQuestions.explanation: A PCB holds the execution state, registers, memory limits, and priority of a process.

quizQuestions.question: What is the action called when the CPU switches from running one process to another?
quizQuestions.explanation: Context switching saves the current state of a process and restores another.

quizQuestions.question: Which synchronization variable manages access to shared resources using signaling?
quizQuestions.explanation: A semaphore is an integer variable accessed via atomic wait and signal operations.

quizQuestions.question: Which page replacement algorithm can experience Belady's Anomaly?
quizQuestions.explanation: In FIFO, increasing page frames can paradoxically increase page faults.

quizQuestions.question: What does the LRU acronym stand for in memory management?
quizQuestions.explanation: LRU stands for Least Recently Used page replacement algorithm.

quizQuestions.question: What is a Zombie process in Unix-like operating systems?
choices: A terminated process whose exit status has not been read by its parent
A process running an infinite loop
A process with no assigned PID
quizQuestions.explanation: A zombie has completed execution but remains in the process table until parent calls wait().

quizQuestions.question: When does an active child process become an Orphan process?
choices: When its parent process terminates before it
quizQuestions.explanation: An orphan process is left running after its parent terminates; it is adopted by init.

quizQuestions.question: Which subsystem commonly uses spooling to manage slow peripheral hardware?
quizQuestions.explanation: Spooling buffers print jobs on disk to prevent blocking application execution.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
quizQuestions.explanation: The TLB is a high-speed hardware cache that speeds up virtual address translation.

quizQuestions.question: What does the `fork()` system call do in Unix-like systems?
choices: Creates a new child process identical to the caller
quizQuestions.explanation: The fork() call creates an almost identical child process by duplicating the caller.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following CPU scheduling algorithms is strictly non-preemptive?
quizQuestions.explanation: FCFS runs each process to completion or until it voluntarily yields.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between a Mutex and a Binary Semaphore?
choices: A Mutex has an ownership concept
A Mutex is implemented purely in software
quizQuestions.explanation: Only the thread that locks a mutex can unlock it, enforcing strict ownership.

quizQuestions.question: Which technique prevents starvation in priority-based CPU scheduling?
quizQuestions.explanation: Aging gradually increases the priority of waiting processes over time.

quizQuestions.question: When does Internal Fragmentation occur in memory management?
choices: When assigned memory is larger than requested
quizQuestions.explanation: Internal fragmentation is unused space within an allocated fixed-size block.

quizQuestions.question: Which memory management approach completely eliminates External Fragmentation?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paging allocates physical memory in fixed-size frames, eliminating external gaps.

quizQuestions.question: What is the guiding design principle of a Microkernel architecture?
choices: Include all OS services in the kernel
Keep only minimal essential services in kernel space
quizQuestions.explanation: Microkernels move non-essential services like file systems into user space.

quizQuestions.question: Which three requirements must a solution to the Critical Section problem satisfy?
quizQuestions.explanation: A valid critical section solution must ensure mutual exclusion, progress, and bounded waiting.

quizQuestions.question: Which process is typically assigned PID 1 in Linux systems?
quizQuestions.explanation: The first user-space process started by the Linux kernel is init (or systemd), having PID 1.

quizQuestions.question: What does Swapping mean in operating system memory management?
choices: Temporarily moving an idle process from RAM to disk
quizQuestions.explanation: Swapping moves an entire process between main memory and secondary storage.

quizQuestions.question: What does the 'A' represent in the database ACID acronym?
quizQuestions.explanation: Atomicity ensures all operations in a transaction succeed or all are rolled back.

quizQuestions.question: Which SQL keyword eliminates duplicate rows from a query result?
quizQuestions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT filters out duplicate tuples from the output relation.

quizQuestions.question: What is a mandatory property of a database Primary Key?
quizQuestions.explanation: Primary keys must uniquely identify each row and cannot be NULL.

quizQuestions.question: What kind of database integrity does a Foreign Key enforce?
quizQuestions.explanation: A foreign key ensures references between child and parent tables remain valid.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary requirement for a table to be in First Normal Form (1NF)?
choices: Every column value must be atomic
quizQuestions.explanation: 1NF requires that all column values are atomic and attributes are not repeating groups.

quizQuestions.question: Which type of dependency must be eliminated to achieve Second Normal Form (2NF)?
quizQuestions.explanation: 2NF requires 1NF and no non-prime attribute depending on a proper subset of a candidate key.

quizQuestions.question: Which type of dependency must be removed to achieve Third Normal Form (3NF)?
quizQuestions.explanation: 3NF requires 2NF and no transitive functional dependencies on non-prime attributes.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following SQL statements is a Data Definition Language (DDL) command?
quizQuestions.explanation: CREATE defines or alters schema structures and is classified as DDL.

quizQuestions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter aggregated group results?
quizQuestions.explanation: The HAVING clause filters groups created by GROUP BY, while WHERE filters individual rows.

quizQuestions.question: Why are indexes created on relational database tables?
choices: To speed up query data retrieval
quizQuestions.explanation: Indexes provide fast lookup paths (like B-trees) that avoid scanning entire tables.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a document-oriented NoSQL database?
quizQuestions.explanation: MongoDB stores flexible JSON-like documents rather than fixed relational tables.

quizQuestions.question: Which symbol represents the Cartesian Product in relational algebra?
quizQuestions.explanation: The cross symbol (X) denotes the Cartesian product of two relations.

quizQuestions.question: What does the Isolation property in ACID guarantee?
choices: Only a single user can log in
quizQuestions.explanation: Isolation guarantees that uncommitted changes from one transaction are invisible to others.

quizQuestions.question: Why is Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) used in database management systems?
choices: To ensure crash recovery and durability
quizQuestions.explanation: WAL records changes to durable log storage before dirty pages are written to tables.

quizQuestions.question: What does the Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol guarantee in databases?
quizQuestions.explanation: Growing and shrinking phases ensure all operations can be serialized cleanly.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary operational difference between TRUNCATE and DELETE in SQL?
choices: TRUNCATE is a faster DDL operation that deallocates data pages
quizQuestions.explanation: TRUNCATE deallocates pages directly without logging individual row deletions.

quizQuestions.question: What is a View in a relational database?
choices: A virtual table defined by a stored query
quizQuestions.explanation: A view does not store data itself; it is a stored query presented as a virtual table.

quizQuestions.question: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) is a stricter version of which normal form?
quizQuestions.explanation: BCNF eliminates remaining functional dependencies where the determinant is not a superkey.

quizQuestions.question: Which geometric shape represents an Entity in an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram?
quizQuestions.explanation: In standard Chen ER notation, entities are drawn as rectangles.

quizQuestions.question: Which shape represents a Relationship in an ER diagram?
quizQuestions.explanation: Relationships connecting entities are depicted using diamonds.

quizQuestions.question: Which SQL join returns only rows that have matching values in both tables?
quizQuestions.explanation: INNER JOIN discards non-matching rows and outputs only matching combinations.

quizQuestions.question: Why is intentional Denormalization sometimes applied in database design?
choices: To optimize read query performance by reducing joins
quizQuestions.explanation: Denormalization adds managed redundancy to avoid expensive join operations on frequent reads.

quizQuestions.question: How many clustered indexes can exist on a single database table?
quizQuestions.explanation: Because a clustered index determines physical storage order, a table can only have one.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a Checkpoint in database transaction recovery?
choices: To flush dirty buffer pages from memory to disk
quizQuestions.explanation: Checkpoints write cached changes to disk, reducing the amount of log replayed after a crash.

quizQuestions.question: How many properties of the CAP theorem can a distributed data store guarantee simultaneously?
quizQuestions.explanation: Under network partition (P), a system must choose between Consistency (C) and Availability (A).

quizQuestions.question: How many layers are in the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) reference model?
quizQuestions.explanation: The OSI model consists of 7 layers from Physical up to Application.

quizQuestions.question: Which networking protocol translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) resolves hostnames to numeric IP addresses.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between TCP and UDP at the transport layer?
quizQuestions.explanation: TCP provides reliable, sequenced delivery via handshakes, whereas UDP is connectionless.

quizQuestions.question: Which default port is used for unencrypted HTTP web traffic?
quizQuestions.explanation: HTTP defaults to port 80, while HTTPS uses port 443.

quizQuestions.question: Which cryptographic protocol is used to encrypt HTTPS communications?
quizQuestions.explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS) encrypts web traffic over HTTPS.

quizQuestions.question: What is the total address length of an IPv4 address in bits?
quizQuestions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits divided into four 8-bit octets.

quizQuestions.question: What is the total bit length of an IPv6 address?
quizQuestions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long and written in hexadecimal notation.

quizQuestions.question: At which layer of the OSI model does an IP router primarily operate?
quizQuestions.explanation: Routers make forwarding decisions based on logical IP addresses at Layer 3 (Network Layer).

quizQuestions.question: Which address does a standard Layer 2 switch use to forward Ethernet frames?
quizQuestions.explanation: Layer 2 switches forward frames based on physical hardware MAC addresses.

quizQuestions.question: Which protocol automatically assigns IP configurations to client devices on a network?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) dynamically leases IP addresses to hosts.

quizQuestions.question: Which protocol is standard for sending outgoing email between mail servers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) handles mail transmission and routing.

quizQuestions.question: What is the packet exchange sequence during a standard TCP three-way handshake?
quizQuestions.explanation: The client initiates with SYN, the server responds with SYN-ACK, and the client acknowledges with ACK.

quizQuestions.question: What is the CIDR prefix notation for the subnet mask 255.255.255.0?
quizQuestions.explanation: 255.255.255.0 has 24 consecutive set bits, represented as /24.

quizQuestions.question: Which protocol does the `ping` command use to check network connectivity?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ping uses ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages.

quizQuestions.question: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to its associated physical MAC address?
quizQuestions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) finds the MAC address corresponding to a known IP.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following IP addresses falls within an RFC 1918 private range?
quizQuestions.explanation: 192.168.0.0/16 is reserved for private local area networks.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary function of Network Address Translation (NAT)?
choices: Mapping private internal IP addresses to a public routable IP
quizQuestions.explanation: NAT maps private local addresses to one or more public IP addresses.

quizQuestions.question: Which media access control protocol was traditionally used in half-duplex Ethernet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ethernet used Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD).

quizQuestions.question: Which protocol is used in 802.11 Wi-Fi networks to manage wireless media access?
quizQuestions.explanation: Wireless networks avoid collisions using Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance.

quizQuestions.question: What is the standard listening port for Secure Shell (SSH) remote administrative access?
quizQuestions.explanation: SSH servers listen on TCP port 22 by default.

quizQuestions.question: How does a network switch differ fundamentally from a network hub?
choices: A switch forwards frames to specific ports, whereas a hub broadcasts to all
A hub operates at full duplex
quizQuestions.explanation: Hubs blindly broadcast frames, while switches inspect MAC addresses to forward frames selectively.

quizQuestions.question: What is the standard Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size for standard Ethernet frames?
quizQuestions.explanation: Standard Ethernet has an MTU payload capacity of 1500 bytes.

quizQuestions.question: Which mechanism does TCP use for end-to-end flow control?
quizQuestions.explanation: TCP uses a dynamic sliding window to prevent the sender from overwhelming receiver buffers.

quizQuestions.question: Which phase begins the TCP congestion control algorithm?
quizQuestions.explanation: TCP connections begin in Slow Start, exponentially doubling the congestion window.

quizQuestions.question: How many ports does traditional FTP use for control and data transfer respectively?
quizQuestions.explanation: FTP uses port 21 for control commands and port 20 for payload data transfer.

quizQuestions.question: Which CPU unit performs arithmetic calculations and logical decisions?
quizQuestions.explanation: The ALU handles all binary arithmetic operations and logical comparisons.

quizQuestions.question: Which storage component offers the fastest access speed in the computer memory hierarchy?
quizQuestions.explanation: CPU registers are built directly into the processor core and offer near-instantaneous access.

quizQuestions.question: What is the defining characteristic of the Von Neumann computer architecture?
choices: Separate data and code memory buses
Shared single memory space for data and instructions
quizQuestions.explanation: Von Neumann systems store both instructions and data in a common address space.

quizQuestions.question: How does the Harvard architecture organize memory compared to Von Neumann?
choices: Uses separate physical memories and buses for data and instructions
quizQuestions.explanation: Harvard architecture isolates instruction pathways from data pathways.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary motivation for CPU instruction pipelining?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pipelining overlaps instruction execution stages to complete instructions each clock cycle.

quizQuestions.question: What does the RISC acronym stand for in computer architecture?
quizQuestions.explanation: RISC stands for Reduced Instruction Set Computer, emphasizing simple, single-cycle instructions.

quizQuestions.question: Which memory technology is predominantly used to implement high-speed CPU cache?
quizQuestions.explanation: SRAM uses flip-flops that do not require periodic refreshing, providing faster access times.

quizQuestions.question: Why does main DRAM (Dynamic RAM) require continuous periodic refresh cycles?
choices: Because memory cell capacitors leak charge over time
quizQuestions.explanation: DRAM stores bits as electrical charges on tiny capacitors that naturally dissipate.

quizQuestions.question: What does the CPU Program Counter (PC) register hold?
choices: The memory address of the next instruction to execute
The base of the current stack frame
quizQuestions.explanation: The Program Counter tracks the memory location of the next sequential instruction.

quizQuestions.question: What is the correct sequential order of the basic CPU instruction cycle?
quizQuestions.explanation: The CPU fetches the instruction, decodes it, executes the operation, and writes back the result.

quizQuestions.question: Which pairs of digital logic gates are considered Universal Gates?
quizQuestions.explanation: Any Boolean function can be constructed exclusively using either NAND or NOR gates.

quizQuestions.question: When does a digital XOR gate produce an output of logic 1?
choices: When the two inputs have different logic values
quizQuestions.explanation: XOR outputs high only when exactly one of its two inputs is high.

quizQuestions.question: What are the outputs produced by a standard digital Half Adder?
quizQuestions.explanation: A half adder adds two 1-bit inputs and outputs both a Sum and a Carry bit.

quizQuestions.question: How many total input bits does a digital Full Adder accept?
quizQuestions.explanation: A full adder adds two operand bits plus an incoming carry-in bit from a previous stage.

quizQuestions.question: What classification does a digital flip-flop circuit belong to?
choices: Sequential Circuit storing 1 bit of state
quizQuestions.explanation: Flip-flops are bistable sequential circuits capable of storing a single binary bit.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary function of a digital Multiplexer (MUX)?
choices: Selects one of several input lines to forward to a single output
Expands a single input to multiple outputs
quizQuestions.explanation: A multiplexer acts as a data selector, routing one chosen input line to its single output.

quizQuestions.question: What does a digital Demultiplexer (DEMUX) do?
choices: Routes a single input signal to one of multiple output lines
quizQuestions.explanation: A demultiplexer distributes a single input line across one selected output channel.

quizQuestions.question: How is the 2's complement of a binary number calculated?
choices: Invert all bits (1's complement) and add 1
quizQuestions.explanation: Taking the 1's complement by inverting bits and adding 1 produces the 2's complement.

quizQuestions.question: What are the three fundamental types of CPU pipelining hazards?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pipeline hazards stem from hardware conflicts (structural), dependencies (data), or branching (control).

quizQuestions.question: Why do modern processors incorporate branch prediction units?
choices: To speed up RAM refresh rates
To avoid pipeline stalls caused by conditional branches
quizQuestions.explanation: Speculating the outcome of branches prevents expensive pipeline flushes.

quizQuestions.question: In a direct-mapped cache, how many cache lines can a specific memory block map to?
quizQuestions.explanation: The cache index bits strictly determine the single line where a given block can reside.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary advantage of a Fully Associative Cache?
choices: Any memory block can be stored in any available cache line
It requires no tag comparison hardware
It eliminates the need for RAM
quizQuestions.explanation: Flexible placement minimizes conflict misses by allowing blocks to occupy any line.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of using a Karnaugh Map (K-map) in digital design?
choices: To simplify Boolean algebra expressions visually
quizQuestions.explanation: K-maps group adjacent truth values to find minimal sum-of-products Boolean expressions.

quizQuestions.question: When do synchronous sequential circuits update their internal state?
choices: Synchronized to a clock edge transition
quizQuestions.explanation: Synchronous circuits update state flip-flops strictly on rising or falling clock edges.

quizQuestions.question: In a Little-Endian computer architecture, where is the Least Significant Byte (LSB) stored?
quizQuestions.explanation: Little-Endian stores the least significant byte of a multi-byte word at the lowest address.

quizQuestions.question: How many secret keys are used in symmetric key cryptography?
choices: Two different public and private keys
quizQuestions.explanation: Symmetric ciphers use the same secret key for both encryption and decryption.

quizQuestions.question: In asymmetric cryptography, which key does a sender use to encrypt a confidential message?
quizQuestions.explanation: Encrypting with the recipient's public key ensures only their private key can decrypt it.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary property of a cryptographic hash function like SHA-256?
choices: It is a one-way mathematical function that cannot be inverted
It can be decrypted with a private key
quizQuestions.explanation: Cryptographic hashes are deterministic one-way functions whose outputs cannot be reversed.

quizQuestions.question: What is the most effective defense against SQL Injection (SQLi) attacks?
quizQuestions.explanation: Prepared statements separate SQL syntax from input data, preventing input from being executed.

quizQuestions.question: What does an attacker execute on a victim's browser during a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack?
quizQuestions.explanation: XSS injects untrusted scripts that execute within the security context of the victim's browser.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary goal of a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack?
choices: To overwhelm target resources and deny service to legitimate users
quizQuestions.explanation: DDoS floods servers with distributed traffic to exhaust network capacity or computing power.

quizQuestions.question: How does a phishing attack typically compromise user accounts?
choices: By using deceptive communication to trick users into revealing credentials
quizQuestions.explanation: Phishing deceives targets with fraudulent messages mimicking trusted entities to steal data.

quizQuestions.question: Which technology prevents Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) eavesdropping on the web?
quizQuestions.explanation: Authenticated TLS establishes an encrypted tunnel that cannot be inspected or altered in transit.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary role of a network firewall?
choices: To inspect and filter network traffic based on configured security rules
quizQuestions.explanation: Firewalls evaluate incoming and outgoing packets against security policies to block unauthorized access.

quizQuestions.question: Why does Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) improve account security?
choices: It removes the need for passwords
It requires an independent secondary factor even if a password leaks
quizQuestions.explanation: 2FA combines something you know (password) with something you possess or are (token/biometric).

quizQuestions.question: Which type of malware locks user files and demands payment to restore access?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts storage and demands a ransom payment for the decryption key.

quizQuestions.question: What security vulnerability occurs when an application writes more data to a buffer than allocated?
quizQuestions.explanation: Buffer overflows overwrite adjacent memory spaces, potentially enabling code execution.

quizQuestions.question: What is the core idea of the Principle of Least Privilege in security design?
choices: Grant each user and process only the minimum permissions necessary
quizQuestions.explanation: Restricting entities strictly to the permissions they require limits breach blast radius.

quizQuestions.question: Which Git command moves modified files from the working directory to the staging area?
quizQuestions.explanation: The `git add` command stages local modifications for inclusion in the next commit snapshot.

quizQuestions.question: What does the `git commit` command record?
choices: A permanent snapshot of staged changes in the local repository
Direct uploads to the remote server
quizQuestions.explanation: Committing stores the currently staged changes as a new commit in the local repository history.

quizQuestions.question: What is the defining characteristic of the Waterfall software development lifecycle?
choices: Strictly sequential phases where each phase completes before the next begins
quizQuestions.explanation: Waterfall enforces a linear sequence from requirements through design, code, and test.

quizQuestions.question: What is a Sprint in the Agile Scrum development framework?
choices: A fixed-length time-boxed iteration producing a shippable increment
quizQuestions.explanation: A sprint is a fixed duration (commonly 1 to 4 weeks) dedicated to completing selected user stories.

quizQuestions.question: What does the 'CI' acronym stand for in modern DevOps pipelines?
quizQuestions.explanation: Continuous Integration automatically merges, builds, and tests code changes regularly.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary scope of Unit Testing in software development?
choices: Testing individual functions or methods in isolation
quizQuestions.explanation: Unit testing validates small, isolated components of code independently.

quizQuestions.question: What information is inaccessible to the tester during Black Box Testing?
choices: Internal source code structure and logic
quizQuestions.explanation: Black box testing examines system behavior without knowledge of internal code or design.

quizQuestions.question: What do engineers inspect during White Box Testing?
choices: Internal logic execution paths, conditions, and code branches
quizQuestions.explanation: White box testing evaluates internal program structures, statements, and control flows.

quizQuestions.question: Why is Regression Testing performed during software maintenance?
choices: To verify that recent code changes have not broken existing functionality
quizQuestions.explanation: Regression testing ensures that fixes or additions have not introduced unintended defects.

quizQuestions.question: What is the central purpose of the Singleton Design Pattern?
choices: To clone multiple instances of a class
To ensure a class has only one instance and provide global access to it
quizQuestions.explanation: Singleton restricts instantiation of a class to a single object across the entire application.

quizQuestions.question: Which design pattern category does the Factory Method pattern belong to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Factory Method handles object creation mechanisms without exposing instantiation logic directly.

quizQuestions.question: What happens when a publisher changes state in the Observer Design Pattern?
choices: All registered observers are automatically notified and updated
quizQuestions.explanation: Observer defines a one-to-many dependency where state changes trigger automatic updates on observers.
